articleTitle: A 3D Fourier split-step technique for modelling microwave propagation in urban areas
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper presents a 3D extension of a full wave propagation model based on the Fourier split-step technique for solving the parabolic approximation to the scalar wave equation. Numerical implementation has been thought for application of propagation in urban areas where effects due to the Earth curvature and to an inhomogeneous atmosphere are negligible. It has been obtained by generalizing the 2D case by means of 2D direct and inverse Fourier transforms and can be used both for a low and a wide angle formulation. Some problematic features related to the necessary boundary conditions for modelling ground and obstacle faces reflections are treated. As examples of application two cases are reported. The first concerns the diffraction by a single perfectly conducting block-shaped building for a vertical and horizontal polarized incident field while the second is a simulation study of what may happen to a point-to-point urban radio link partially obstructed by the presence of a building when a second one is added close to the first.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of radio relay link performance using a deterministic 3D wave propagation model
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Presents an approach for the prediction of radio relay link performance (probability distribution of path loss and IBLAD) and diversity improvement parameters (space, angle, pattern diversity) under varying tropospherical propagation conditions (k-factor-statistics, refractive index structure). Based on a deterministic 3D wave propagation model, the statistical behavior of the propagation conditions is simulated for varying input parameters according to available meteorological statistics. The wave propagation model takes into account scattering and diffraction in the vertical transmitter-receiver plane, and in addition rough surface scattering in the real three-dimensional environment. A digital terrain database for topographical and morphographical information is applied. The influence of the atmosphere is modeled with respect to k-factor-statistics, or, if the refractive index structure is available, by a ray-tracing algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measured improvements using angle and space diversity on a terrestrial microwave radio link
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: In order to measure the error performance of angle diversity (AD) and space diversity (SD) systems a field trial is in progress on a 52.9 km hop between Karlstad and Filipstad, situated in the western part of Sweden. The transmission quality of the digital radio system with both space and angle diversity configurations is measured simultaneously and the observed bit error ratios for these configurations are compared with a single unprotected channel. One important condition for this experiment is to use AD antennas at both stations, i.e. transmitting and receiving should take place in the same antenna.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Economics of local loop competition by radio access
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Describes the economics of radio access in the local loop, compares the attractiveness of competing technologies and concludes that there are no general solutions. Each potential service area must be analysed separately in order to determine the optimum mix of technologies. In general radio based technologies appear best suited to low population density areas with GSM solutions appropriate for widespread rural areas and DCS1800 suited to village and small town environments, DECT based systems become more attractive with increasing traffic density. However, fully cabled solutions can be cheaper than radio-based ones in areas of high population density, particularly where mobility is not required.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Proposal for modulation level controlled radio system applied to ATM networks
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Analyzes the cell loss performance of the modulation level controlled radio system applied to ATM networks. This system increases total transmissible capacity by controlling the number of modulation levels, so can effectively absorb traffic fluctuation occurring in ATM networks and reduce cell loss probability. As a result of analysis, it was found that the proposed system can drastically reduce ATM cell loss to about 1/100 approximately 1/1000, compared with the conventional virtual path (VP) capacity fixed transmission system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Equivalence relations between angle diversity and other diversity methods. Analytical model and practical results
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Diversity reception is an efficient means to improve signal quality or to reduce outage time in radio-relay systems. Already well known from application in analogue and digital systems are space diversity (SD) and frequency diversity (FD). Also, angle diversity (AD) has found increasing interest for radio-relay due to its main advantages: need of one Rx-antenna only, and no waste of frequency band. Practical use of any countermeasure however depends on reliable planning tools which allow prediction of system performance and outage. One approach to make the efficiency of diversity predictable is to analyze correlation between main path and diversity path and to describe it by a correlation coefficient (CC). Analogies are developed between both FD and AD and SD and AD. Based on these analogies equivalence relations are derived analytically which allow one to compute the CC of AD from the better known and experimentally verified CCs of SD and FD.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Methods for ascertaining radar interference into high capacity radio relay receivers
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The operational surveillance of radio relay equipment carrying normal traffic has become common within many administrations. The parity check feature of the radio frame is exploited to derive an estimate of the bit error rate (BER) and subsequently the number of events (seconds) when a certain BER is exceeded is cumulated. Thus one may estimate whether the performance of a particular transceiver/radio hop will meet the requirements of CCIR Rec. G.821. The function described is performed by the supervisory system for all radio channels and all hops of a particular transmission system. Some methods for ascertaining the occurrence of radar EMI, and for extracting some of the characteristic features of an interfering radar are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: First results of the 16/64 QAM XPIC trial in the Netherlands
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: A description of a 16/64 QAM XPIC trial in the Netherlands is given. Two 16/64 QAM co-channel pairs, one of which is equipped with XPICs, are monitored to obtain the performance improvement by XPICs. From measurements over two years it follows that a reduction in outage time (BER greater than 10/sup -3/) of approximately 2 to 4 can be obtained for both 16 and 64 QAM modulation. XPICs also reduce the unavailable time considerably. Because part of the unavailable time is converted to severely errored seconds, the improvement factor in SES is somewhat lower than the reduction in outage time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Access radio systems in SDH and mobile networks
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: A new access radio family is described, pointing out basic concepts, innovative technologies and overall performance. The radio application in access links appears as a most promising one to be adopted in modern, rapidly evolving telecommunication networks. Examples of application in SDH and in mobile networks are examined in particular, showing the main technical features and a number of operating advantages. A first implementation is finally presented, specially referring to the outdoor unit developed for a STM-1/18 GHz system, offering a full SDH functionality in the access network with an extremely compact structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Video transmission using millimetre wave radio systems
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The development of a video distribution system in the 28 GHz band by BT started in 1986 to meet the demand for a radio system that could provide the final link to customers to make available a satellite service where customers could not have direct satellite reception for a number of reasons. Subsequently the system has been adapted to also provide point-to-point closed circuit TV applications. At the same time, a demonstration of multichannel TV delivery directly to homes was established by BT Laboratories at Saxmundham in Suffolk in the 28 GHz band.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modem for a PMP radio system using trellis coded modulation with burst transmission
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: A new family of modems for point-to-multipoint (PMP) systems is described, designed to improve frequency utilisation, power economy and transmission quality. The key technique is the application of the trellis coded modulation (TCM), which gives a coding gain compared to uncoded modulation schemes, thus resulting in higher system gain and/or lower transmit power (RF and DC). However the applicability of the TCM to burst operation, which is needed in such TDMA systems, is not obvious. This contribution describes, how the modem is built up and how digital signal processing lead to a clear, flexible and powerful design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new differential adaptive modem for multipath propagation
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The presence of intersymbol interference due to multipath propagation in a digital radio transmission tends to degrade considerably the performance of the receiver. In order to compensate for the unknown channel and time varying linear distorsion, adaptive equalizers are frequently used in efficient digital communication systems. Differentially coherent reception does not require sophisticated carrier recovery circuits and it is tolerant to the multipath propagation phenomena. In addition, it is particularly insensitive to local oscillator microphony thus enabling it to work in a severe environment. Finally, it gives satisfactory performance with a very simple receiver. The author presents a modem, based on a new adaptive equalizer for differentially coherent receiver proposed by Sehier and Kawas Kaleh (1990). Descriptions of original diversity combiner and clock signal phase estimation are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low-cost high performance radio-link antennas for 23/26/28/38 GHz frequency bands
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The utilization of frequency bands above 20 GHz for short distance digital radio links requires relatively small antennas (diameter less than one meter) adapted to the particular frequency band. Due to the competitive market situation the antennas have to be very cheap in series production. Furthermore, the antennas have to meet the system relevant stringent electrical requirements concerning reflection coefficients and the radiation pattern envelopes. In 1992, the ETSI published parameters of radio relay systems operating at 23, 26 and 38 GHz bands, among them antenna radiation pattern envelopes. According to local interference requirements antennas with moderate or very stringent sidelobe suppression may be necessary. Based on these requirements, an antenna family has been developed, which allows an easy adaption to different frequency bands and sidelobe requirements using low-cost components and technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An evolutionary approach to the management of SDH radio equipments
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: A number of radio relay and fibre optic systems are required to be remotely controlled and monitored. Year by year customer's requirements are becoming more and more demanding in order to achieve an effective supervision of the network. With SDH equipment these requirements are becoming even more complex to be satisfied. The paper illustrates Siemens Telecomunicazioni's approach to provide a satisfactory solution to customer's needs on this topic. In particular, after introducing the main characteristics of present supervisory systems for PDH networks are the way to reach a future fully standardised SDH management, an SDH radio equipment is described from the management point of view. The ability of the new equipment generation to be adopted by the old generation of supervisory systems and then to evolve towards a new management philosophy with just software enhancements and minor hardware improvements, is also illustrated. The process for the integration of radio and fibre Optic Equipment of different vendors in a single management network is described and a step by step approach explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wireless access based on CT-2 radio system
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Several potential technologies have been evaluated for wireless access, including CT-2, DECT and a number of proprietary systems. In most cases it is clear that the system architecture can be independent of the radio technology. To meet the objective of low costs, the proposed system has been based upon a standard radio interface thus allowing volume of scale cost reductions to be achieved. The prototype wireless access system is based on CT-2 as this technology is already in volume production. The architecture of the wireless access system is compatible with DECT and, when this technology is commercially available, it would be possible to upgrade the wireless access system to provide basic rate ISDN. The CT-2 radio distribution point (DP) provides 6 radio channels which can support up to 30 customers by employing demand assignment. The 6 radio transceivers communicate with the supporting exchange interface equipment via 3 copper pairs using digital transmission based on the ISDN U interface. A key requirement when designing the radio DP is to minimise the power consumption so that the unit can be powered over the same three copper pairs used for transmission. To achieve this it is necessary to minimise the functionality at the radio DP and make best use of the signalling channel on the U interface to control the transceivers from the exchange interface.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of LMS adaptive filtering for PMP radio system applications
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Point to multipoint (PMP) radio systems normally operate in propagation environments where significant delay spreads may be encountered due to the fact that, in base stations, sectorial or even omnidirectional aerials are employed. In most of the cases there is a line of sight link but, because of lateral/ground reflections and because most of the times neither antenna can be mounted clear of local clutter, sometimes there is a high possibility of multipath dispersion. In point to point systems the solutions to avoid the multipath phenomena are well known: space, frequency or even angle diversity and adaptative equalizers. The present paper considers time domain adaptative equalizers (ATDE) in a PMP TDMA environment. A comparison between different equalization methods is made, always in a TDMA environment. Some considerations over the fixed point realization of the schemes are presented; and its physical implementation is contemplated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Air interface considerations for wireless LANs
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The growing demand for wireless access to local area networks (LANs) is currently stimulating much work in the field of radio LANs (RLANs). The paper discusses the various options for the RLAN, alongside implementation feasibility. The advantages and disadvantages of each scheme are highlighted and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A compact BCM modem implementation for SDH access radio
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The SDH access radio network calls today for a modem that is properly implemented. Neither the simplicity of a 4-PSK modem, nor the sophisticated multilevel high capacity modems with their expensive power consumption are suitable. The authors think that the compactness, the low power consumption, the right spectrum efficiency associated with a good receiver sensitivity and consequently a low cost are the requisites of such a modem. Their aims are attainable only with the best trade-off between shaping, mode modulation and coding techniques. A 16-BCM modem implementation is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hardware realization of an XPIC system/measurement method and results
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: A new generation of 64 QAM radio relay systems developed for the transmission of SDH- and PDH- signals has been presented by Geidel et al. (1991). The most advanced version from the technical point of view as well as with respect to cost effectiveness and frequency economy was a system with quadruple carrier transmission, using both frequency and polarization multiplex techniques with cross polarization interference cancellers (XPIC). A more detailed description is given of the modulators and demodulators mentioned in this context, the concepts of which have been slightly modified. Furthermore measurement methods and results are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implications of draft new ITU-T Recommendation G.826 on digital radio-relay systems
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Draft new ITU-T Recommendation G.826 specifies error performance parameters and objectives for international digital paths at or above the primary rate. These paths may be based on a PDH, SDH or some other transport network. Future radio-relay systems, which will form part of these paths have to comply with this recommendation. The present paper analyzes the new concepts introduced in G.826 and applies them to radio-relay systems. It will be shown that the performance requirements of G.826 are more stringent than those in the present recommendations based on G.821. This may result in a reduction of the achievable hop lengths; several calculated examples are given. Lastly, some countermeasures to overcome the limitations of G.826 are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frame selector (for combining parallel data channels)
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Frame selection is a method used to combine parallel data channels in order to achieve lowest possible error rate. This method has significant improvement potential compared to conventional switching techniques and early warning systems. The frame selection technique also improves the residual bit error rate since it works at every error rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Results of the Detailed Spectrum Investigation (DSI)
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Presents the results of the Detailed Spectrum Investigation (DSI) which has been initiated by the European Radio Office (ERO) the permanent body of the European Radiocommunications Committee (ERC), one of the working groups of the CEPT. The author first gives a reminder of the present structure of the CEPT. Then the development of the DSI process is explained. The DSI recommendations are given and the author comments on the table of frequency allocations and utilisations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experimental results from a 70 Mbit/s-16 QAM 229 km oversea radio link in Italy
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper reports the experimental results obtained during a first trial period, September 1992 to July 1993, for a digital radio-relay link over the Mediterranean sea between Sardinia and the Continent in Italy. In order to achieve the required level of performance the system configuration was designed to use space (with in-phase maximum power combiners, IPMAP) and frequency diversities with three operating frequencies per direction (early warning driven hitless switching). During the first trial period a new optimized IF combiner prototype was also tested on one channel in order to verify the improving on the space diversity performance. The new combiner uses a new strategy optimized for error probability reduction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Considerations on SDH radio relay systems management
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Highlights some management aspects related to SDH digital radio relay systems (SDH DRRS in the next), in order to allow a full integration between SDH DRRS and other SDH network elements. The analysis deals with STM-1 radio relay systems, but it can be extended without significant modifications to other transport levels (sub-STM-1, STM-4, etc.). The following, basic structure of SDH management system planned for SIP network is briefly discussed, in terms of the architecture and information model. Then general guidelines suitable for a full integrated DRRS management are proposed. In particular issues related to identification of SDH DRRS with 'network element' (NE) are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Results of 2 year measurements on a 18 GHz radio link: rain unavailability considerations for radio relay systems at low and high capacity
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The use of radio frequencies for transmission and reception of digital signals above 10 GHz is practically limited by the effect of rain. The water drops adsorb and diffuse the radio signal, producing an attenuation that increases with rain intensity and depth of the rain cell. The system becomes unavailable when this attenuation equals its FFM, (flat fade margin) producing BER >or=10/sup -3/, for 10 consecutive seconds at least. Since rain phenomena usually last more than 10 seconds, it's important to obtain the relationship between the rain fallen and the unavailability expected, in order to correctly design the radio links. A comparison is done between the values expected from two largely used prediction methods and the measured values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TMN aspects regarding radio relay systems for SDH and PDH signals
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: For SDH transmission equipment a TMN system is nearly mandatory. Thereby it is indispensable that all equipment concerned is managed by a common TMN system. Transmission equipment for that are add drop multiplexers (ADMX), fibre optic (FO)- and radio transmission systems for SDH signals. But also existing PDH equipment should be included into TMN as far as possible. Some aspects of a QD2-application on a SDH-radio relay system are treated with a view to a migration strategy to a CCITT conformable TMN interface.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Loss of pointer in SDH digital radio relay systems
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The use of synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) in digital radio relay systems (DRRS) requires the analysis of the effect of error statistics on the transmission frame. In fact, due to the recent adoption in high capacity SDH DRRSs of transmission techniques such as low redundancy error-correcting codes, trellis coded modulations, Viterbi receivers, etc., the errors produced in the presence of noise tend to be clustered in bursts. The occurrence in the SDH transmission systems of error bursts may cause severe malfunctioning, such as, for example, the loss of a virtual container due to the incorrect detection of a pointer. In order to evaluate the loss of pointer probability due to errors, as defined in CCITT Rec. G.709 and G.783, it is necessary to know the error distribution in a time interval of N bits. The paper first describes the new model adopted to represent the error distribution and the probability to have an incorrect detection of a pointer. Then, the results obtained by means of a such new model are presented and compared with those obtained by both simulation and measurements, using the above-mentioned transmission techniques. Finally, the characteristics of the simulated transmission system and measurement set-up are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of VHDL for the whole design flow of digital radio devices
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: VHDL, the IEEE-standard hardware description language, is achieving popularity among digital electronics designers as an input for automatic synthesis tools, which are able to convert abstract descriptions into logic. However, VHDL can be used for much more ambitious tasks in the design process, and finds application throughout the whole design flow, including specification-VHDL was conceived to merely do so-, high-level simulation and evaluation of the complete system, even if analog blocks are involved, lower-level description of the digital devices for their automatic synthesis, and effortless documentation of the hardware designed. The paper presents a real-life VHDL design experience, as a means to discuss the pros and cons of this new methodology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A STM-1 radio relay equipment for transmission in frequency bands with about 30 MHz channel spacing
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Summarises some of the results achieved by utilising trellis coded modulation (TCM) combined with Viterbi decoding and a strong adaptive time domain equalizer (ATDE) in a radio relay equipment for transmission of a STM-1 signal (155 Mbit/s). The equipment is available in all frequency bands from 4 to 13 GHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis and simulation of a distributed rural radiotelephone network
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper presents the results of simulations of a self configuring radio system using packet radio techniques to set up duplex circuits, which has many advantages for the provision of telephone services in rural areas of developing countries. It is justifiable to consider blocking on this type of network as being described by the order of the network consisting of the stations not being used at any instant for carrying traffic. So long as this is over some magic number the blocking is adequately small. Increasing the order can be achieved if necessary by increasing power and antenna height. However this has the disadvantage of causing congestion on the traffic channels. There is therefore much to be gained by the use of efficient routing algorithms which approach the theoretical limit based on whether stations are in disconnected sets, without generating undue amounts of traffic on the calling channel. Simulation results have been presented for a simple algorithm which shows promise but has too high a 'magic number'. Analysis is performed to show how this can be improved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technical and economic assessment on radio relay systems in the local and distribution Italian networks
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Presents a technical and economic assessment on digital radio relay systems (DRRSs) for the Italian local and distribution network. The authors summarize the evolution trends for the Italian local and distribution network, outlining the modification of network structure to understand the possible application field of DRRSs. They deal with the role of the DRRSs for the introduction of SDH systems and architectures in the loop. Finally, they show the main results of an economic comparison between DRRSs and optical technology in local and distribution network for the case of ring topology and point-to-point solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Millimetric wave systems-the attractive access radio solution
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Considers millimetric systems to be those operating above 20 GHz which coincides with the definition used by ETSI for ETS specification activities. The work by ETSI at present covers the 20-60 GHz range with transmission rates from 2-155 Mbit/s. The paper also examines the likely applications for millimetric links, the propagation differences not normally considered in lower frequency bands to be important and the product concepts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Planar sector-beam antenna for point to multipoint systems around and above 10 GHz
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: After justifying the choice of radiation pattern for an antenna dedicated to point to multipoint systems above 10 GHz, the article describes the design of such an antenna working at 23 GHz. Planar printed antennas are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 58 GHz technology and experimental link
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Trends in military and civilian communication systems lead to the increasing use of millimeter wave frequencies. Among those the 60 GHz band is particularly interesting due to the atmospheric absorption (frequency reuse, discretion). Alcatel Telspace has studied millimeter waves technologies allowing the development of a new millimeter wave products generation. The paper describes the results of this work and its application on a 58 GHz test link with data bit rates of 2 and 8 Mbit/s.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving SDH radio quality performance: the WEST combiner concept and benefits for space diversity receivers
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Discusses a new and effective approach to describe QAM system performance in high capacity SDH radio as a function of properly weighted power level and spectrum distortion. An efficient combiner for space diversity receivers, based on these concepts-the WESt (Weighted Evaluation Strategy) combiner-is also described, and simulation and laboratory measurements on prototypes are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spread spectrum wireless links
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper explains the basic technology of spread spectrum modulation. An application provides licence-free 'instant' wireless links under Part 15 of the FCC Rules in the USA. Western Multiplex has designed a spread spectrum digital microwave radio with a standard Tl/El interface for a private point-to-point service. This radio performs very effectively in the presence of interference, dispersive fading and with poor RF antenna impedance matching.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Propagation on 23, 31 and 50 GHz line-of-sight over-water paths
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Propagation investigations have been performed during a period of three years (1988-1990) on the east coast of Sweden. The primary purpose of the measurements was to establish the limitations in availability caused by fading due to rain, snow, multipath propagation, hail and fog. Prediction models (CCIR) for rain and multipath fading have been adapted, monthly and annually, to experimental cumulative distributions of fade depth. The influence of hail, fog and multipath propagation showed to be of minor importance. In summary, the performance was clearly limited by rain and snow fading.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Narrow band modulation and coding schemes for radio LAN
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper considers the performance of narrow-band modulation schemes on the indoor radio channel, such as occurs in radio LAN systems. This channel is subject to i.s.i. due to multipath, which limits the maximum data rate. The paper proposes narrow-band modulation and coding to reduce the symbol rate. The paper compares the performances of multilevel signalling constellations of different rates, and shows that the intersymbol interference and hence the irreducible error rate floor are reduced by higher rate multilevel modulation as compared with QPSK, provided the signalling pulse width, and therefore the signal bandwidth, is kept constant. It is also shown that diversity techniques are important in the indoor communications scenario.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Impact of Recommendation G.826 on the system design of radio relay systems
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper first discusses the development of the new ITU-TSS (CCITT) error performance Recommendation G.826 and the subsequent development by ITU-RS (CCIR) Study Group 9 of a preliminary draft new Recommendation aligned to G.826. The paper then considers the stringency and impact of the new SG9 Recommendation on the system design of digital radio-relay systems (DRS) and the complexity and cost for DRS to deliver similar error performance to that of fibre optic transmission systems (FOTS). The preliminary conclusions from current TELSTRA SDH-DRS field trials and the aims and configuration of a new trial are also briefly summarised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A single chip adaptive QAM processor for data rates up to 500 Mbit/s
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The miniaturization of CMOS structures allows the realization of a complex-valued adaptive time domain equalizer at a symbol rate of 30 MHz on one VLSI chip by using the 'application specific' gate array technique (ASICs). By making use of a full custom design and CMOS technology it was possible to integrate on one chip not only an entire complex-valued baseband transversal equalizer but also all the important hardware needed to perform the digital signal processing functions of a typical QAM receiver used for high capacity digital radio. The chip application covers 16 QAM(TCM) to 1024 QAM(TCM) and it can be operated with a maximum symbol speed of 60 MBaud. It comprises an adaptive time domain equalizer, a frequency domain slope equalizer, the digital parts of timing and carrier recovery loops, FM interference suppressor and some useful housekeeping functions (offset control, AGC). It can also be used for crosspolarization interference cancellation (XPIC).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assessments of the impact of CCITT G.826 Recommendation on radio relay system design and radio link deployments
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper presents an analysis of the impact of the new CCITT Rec. G.826 on digital radio transmission. In this respect, it appears quite important to define suitable allocation criteria and the paper depicts two possible allocation rules. It is confirmed that the new quality objectives are all more stringent that the G.821 corresponding ones. Radio systems' technological evolution, however, can allow compliance with these more severe objectives without important modification of the actual system infrastructure and architecture. As a consequence no special effort is considered to be required when planning future digital radio on existing infrastructures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Error-correction techniques and adaptive linearization in SDH radio
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: In high capacity digital radio-relay systems (DRRSs) it is necessary to make use of complex modulation schemes (e.g. 32-, 64-, 128-, 256- or even 512-QAM) to achieve desired spectral efficiency. These modulation schemes are particularly sensitive to many types of impairments and their use requires sophisticated techniques to deal with some of them. The article describes two countermeasures used to improve performances and to face problems related to noise and nonlinear distortions, respectively. It refers to a SDH DRRS, which uses 128-QAM modulation to carry a STM-1 payload in frequency bands with 28 to 30 MHz channel spacing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent technical and regulatory developments affecting the UK fixed services frequency bands
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: There have been a number of concurrent technical and regulatory developments affecting UK users of fixed service spectrum. As the body responsible for efficient spectrum management in the UK, the Radiocommunications Agency (RA) has been working closely with equipment manufacturers and network operators to respond effectively to these developments. The paper reviews the key developments affecting demand for and availability of fixed service spectrum in the UK and outlines how industry and the regulatory authorities are responding to the changes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multipoint radio systems: planning tools using terrain data bases derived from satellite remote sensing
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Describes how the satellite derived terrain data bases can be used as a planning aid in the development of a multipoint radio system and to analyse the feasibility of such data. The main advantages of satellite derived terrain data are their availability in a relatively short period of time and the spatial resolution (up to 10 m) which is suitable to represent urban areas. The analysis of the radio coverage of a nodal station (NS) has been carried out in terms of the percentage of visibility within a given area (1*1 km). Each NS is characterized by a distribution of this visibility estimator computed for the whole coverage region. It is responsibility of the system designer the choice of the most appropriate parameter of the statistical distribution (average percentage visibility, minimum value, etc.) for the evaluation of the coverage quality.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The benefit of cross-polar co-channel operation in digital radio networks
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Digital radio systems with co-channel operation are a powerful and economic transport medium for modern transmission networks. Thereby co-channel operation provides an extremely efficient use of radio frequency resources, offers economical solutions for capacity extensions and re-utilization of existing infrastructure, and gives advantages in densely meshed radio networks. The performance and reliability of the co-channel concept are confirmed through more than seven years of field experience.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

Index Terms: Years Of Experience In The Field

articleTitle: Optimum hop length for millimeteric wave radio links in arid land climate
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Reliability analysis of millimetric wave radio links operating in an arid climate are presented and used to derive the hop length versus fade margin charts. Long term rain and visibility data for Saudi Arabia, are used to determine rain and visibility statistics for various regions of the country. Based on the results of measured attenuation at 40 GHz in Riyadh, meteorological statistics are converted into excess attenuation due to rain, sandstorms and multipath fading. Finally, the total outage time due to the three phenomenon is depicted as a function of fade margin at various hop lengths. The result is a set of design charts which relate hop lengths, reliability objectives and fade margins for various climates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The integration of digital microwave radio systems under the telecommunications management network (TMN)
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: From the outset of synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) was designed as a managed telecommunications transmission network and, as such, embodied the principles of the telecommunications management network (TMN) in the design of its management infrastructure. The TMN provides an alarm and performance monitoring capability and offers configuration and inventory management functions. It enables flexible provisioning of circuits and facilitates signal protection by re-routing. These features should lead to optimum network utilisation, improved availability and a reduction in operating costs. The authors summarise and explain the principles behind TMN and examine its applicability to microwave radio. They also consider various radio architectures and identifies suitable network element models for efficient management of digital radio systems. As SDH digital radio relay systems should be fully integrated into the SDH network, future standardisation activities must define relevant functional blocks and information models for radio systems that are equivalent to models used in fibre optic systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 38 GHz transceiver design: a choice
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: With the sudden boom of high frequency applications, such as those in the 38 GHz band, design engineers are facing the choice between different RF technologies whilst fulfilling time to market constraints and high volume production requirements. This problem is mainly related to the transmit signal generation. After a brief review of the main relevant available technologies the article makes use of an actual example of equipment under production and how it can gradually evolve in the future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A N+2 protection switching system for synchronous STM-1 signals and plesiochronous 140 Mbit/s signals by using two carrier technique
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The availability of a high capacity radio link mainly depends on the reliability of the radio system and the occurrence of fading events. For improving availability and quality of a radio relay link there are protection channels added to the operating channels. In the configuration 1+1 one protection channel is assigned to each operating channel. In the configuration n+2 two protection channels are provided for up to n operating channels. The article describes a protection switching system which was designed for line protection. The system is able to handle STM-1 signals (155 Mbit/s) as well as plesiochronous 140 Mbit/s signals. All special requirements concerning two-carrier systems were taken into consideration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The DECT standard in local loop access applications
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper discusses the suitability of the Digital European Cordless Telecommunications (DECT) radio interface for use in a wireless local loop (WLL) application. The relevance of this standard for WLL applications is highlighted, particularly with respect to the likely service requirements and attributes of these local access networks. The paper concludes with an example of a potential DECT WLL architecture.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of a 64 QAM radio using digital filters with small rolloffs
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The increasing demand for transmission capacity of public and private networks and the limited availability of radio frequencies is the major driving force behind the search for microwave radio concepts with high spectral efficiency. In the past this has led to the design of systems with increasingly higher modulation levels, with the bulk of modern high capacity digital microwave radios employing a 64 QAM modulation scheme. Based on a commercially available 64 QAM, 155 Mbit/s radio system, investigations were carried out to explore the limits of enhancing spectral efficiency by employing pulse shaping filters with small rolloffs. Comparisons were made to a standard system equipped with surface acoustic wave (SAW) filters with a rolloff factor of 34%. By switching from the SAW filter in the modulator to a digital filter, without any need for further modifications, satisfactory system performance could be sustained even at rolloffs as low as 15%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Opportunities for Sub STM-1 radio systems in the BT network
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper outlines applications for Sub STM-1 radio systems within the BT United Kingdom network and provides information for discussion within the ITU and ETSI forums towards standardisation of SDH systems below STM-0 (VC-3). It outlines the benefits of functional integration of SDH radio systems and add drop multiplexers (ADM). It also provides a brief overview of BT's UK synchronous transmission network and identifies potential applications for sub STM-1 systems. The paper discusses means of achieving very high availability and reliability standards for business customers, including duplication of serving sites links to customers premises, dual parenting from different serving sites, or via parallel access to different outer core rings. Finally, it gives a summary of typical system parameters for combined SDH Access Radio and multiplexer systems at STM-0 (VC-3 or 21*2 Mbit/s) with options for different types of interfaces.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: One per customer digital radio system
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper briefly reviews the development of the one per customer (1pC) concept up to the implementation of the technology trial. The trial equipment is described and initial results from propagation testing are discussed. The 1pC direct sequence CDMA trial system configuration has successfully demonstrated its ability to offer a 160 kb/s digital bearer suitable for analogue telephony service to four fixed RNUs and one transportable RNU. The 1pC system was capable of providing coverage to a significant proportion of the Stoke Mandeville exchange area. Successful diffracted path operation was demonstrated for paths of less than 5 km. A clear line of sight path of 18 km was demonstrated for the 1pC system with performance better than BER 10/sup -8/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new acquisition technique for carrier recovery with QAM signals
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Describes a frequency error detector (FED) for all modulation systems using quadratic modulation schemes, such as 16-QAM, 64-QAM, 256-QAM and so on. Its main advantage is the very high resistance to all kinds of signal faults such as distortions, level errors or noise. Simultaneously, it permits a high acquisition range to be achieved (more than Delta f/fs=5% in noise-free environments). Typical applications of the new FED are data transmissions over fading channels without using preambles or other additional aids for carrier acquisition. For this reason, very economical XPIC structures become possible. The method described here can be regarded as an advanced development of the FEDs presented by Sari and Moridi (1988).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 2nd generation of millimetre-wave point-to-point digital systems
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Until now, UK has been the primary market for millimetre-wave point-to-point digital links, corresponding to a first generation of systems. At present, the millimetre-wave market is enlarging its borders to other European countries while evolving. The market evolution is analysed together with the evolution of the corresponding technology. The analysis leads to the identification of new features and of a new architecture for the design of millimetre-wave systems, which are the basis of 2nd generation systems developed by Alcatel.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Blind algorithms for joint clock recovery and baseband combining in digital radio
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: A strategy is illustrated for joint space diversity baseband combining and timing recovery in microwave digital radio, based on a phase-independent criterion. The proposed receiver both provides a steady-state performance close to minimum mean square error receiver and solves the problems related to system synchronization, with an effective synergic action of clock recovery and adaptive baseband combining. The only multipath fading event which produces a (potential) system outage is given by two channels with only a slight difference in both notch frequency and notch depth. In this case, the post-combining equalizer is still able to equalize channels of moderate notch depth. The novelty of the present study is the joint application of the constant modulus algorithm to clock recovery and baseband combining. As a result, a significant immunity of the sampler/combiner on carrier phase is achieved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 60 GHz transmission experiment in the Netherlands
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Describes the results of a 60 GHz transmission experiment conducted in the Netherlands and the radio equipment developed by PTT Research for experimental purposes. The experiment revealed that the higher millimetre wave bands, in particular the 60 GHz band, offer significant potential for local communications. The CCIR model for rain attenuation was found to be useful for modelling this type of transmission system for frequencies up to and including 60 GHz. However, the wide fluctuations in annual and worst-month rain statistics may be a source of concern for the service provider.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of an urban point-to-multipoint millimetric radio system with a two level hierarchy
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The design of a flexible urban point-to-multipoint (P-MP) network architecture is proposed. A two level hierarchical cellular structure is introduced that takes advantage of propagation conditions in two recently opened millimetric frequency bands. This leads to improvements over existing systems that employ single size cells. The proposed network judiciously deploys large and small cells and different uplink/downlink frequency pairs in a sector. This increases flexibility in deployment and improves reconfigurability to changing subscriber demands. It also provides a means of controlling congestion. As a result, decreased bandwidth requirement per uplink/downlink pair may be achieved. Consequently power requirements on the radio hardware are reduced. Alternatively the extra power can be used to combat the commonly experienced problem of rain fading.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multicarrier modulation technique for wireless local area networks
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: The paper proposes the multicarrier modulation/differential detection technique for wireless local area networks. One computationally efficient closed form expression for the bit error rate in a frequency- and time-selective Rayleigh fading channel is derived, and numerical results to show the BER performance in a practical indoor wireless channel are demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advanced SDH radio systems for transport of STM-1
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Describes advanced long haul SDH radio systems operating with 30 and 40 MHz channel spacing. To achieve high quality and robust radio systems, newly developed key technologies such as multi-level coded modulation (MLCM) and decision feedback equalization (DFE) are applied. Their main features, performance and measured data are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RF modem for high capacity radio system
publicationTitle: 1993 Fourth European Conference on Radio Relay Systems
abstract: Presents a new high-capacity microwave system in the upper 6 GHz band based on microwave modulation and demodulation. This equipment is designed in two versions, organised around a common TX/RX, and differing only in the framing and error code correction modules. The first version transmits the highest level (140 Mbit/s) of plesiochronous digital hierarchy (PDH) and uses 16QAM modulation. The second version transmits an STM-1 signal (first level of the synchronous digital hierarchy-SDH). This version is originally intended for use in an SDH network but can be used in a transitory step to transmit 140 Mbit/s signals, mapped into an STM-1 frame. It is based on 32 TCM-4D coded modulation. The paper focuses mainly on the RF modules, addressing MMIC (monolithic microwave integrated circuit) products as an alternative to discrete ones. It presents their relationship with signal processing, including original solutions that have been devised for high level RF modulation and demodulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
